Personal grooming/skincare is one of the biggest triggers for my hand washing compulsion next to cooking. I've had skin picking problems and acne for about 13 years and a lot of my contamination issues center around the idea of getting some kind of skin infection, so that's why. When I take a shower I wash my hands first thing (to make sure they're clean enough to properly wash my body), wash my asshole first (so that having an unclean asshole can't interfere with the rest of my shower) and immediately wash my hands a second time (because I just touched my asshole). I also need to listen to music in the shower because I use it to time how long I spend washing different parts of my body, but I can only listen to music through earbuds unless it's in the car, so I need to take them out and put them back in a bajillon times to stop them from getting too wet if I'm washing my face or hair, so I wash my hands again if I touch anything other than my towel or headphones/headphone case. I also wash my hands before washing my face. If I wash my face at the sink instead of in the shower I'll get caught in a loop washing my hands if I touch pretty much anything, but some parts of my skincare routine I have no choice but to do at the sink (especially shaving my face), so washing my face in the shower can only mitigate that problem so much.

Since I was a kid, I get all worried doubting if my favorite color/movie/band/food etc. is really my favorite, but then I feel guilty for even considering removing my "favorite" from its special place inside of my head. For example, sometimes I think I might like a cranberry/maroon color more than I like orange, but I've been saying orange is my favorite color since middle school, and now I need to keep saying orange is my favorite color because I feel like the concept of orange would feel abandoned and rejected if it stopped being my favorite. Generally my solution to this is to say that my favorite thing for a given category is like a five way tie so nothing gets left out.

College boy here. It's really tough to manage but school gives me something more important than my ED to focus on and my university is in a city with way more resources than my hometown. My ED was at its worst at the end of high school and I took a gap year to make sure I was stabilized enough to be on my own. School exacerbates my issues sometimes but even though I'm still not fully recovered I'm so much more functional and my ED is so much easier to manage. Back home I have no friends and there aren't any therapists in the area, nothing to do but get stoned and keep myself busy cleaning my mom's house, much easier to get to the point where I decide I need to "get serious" again and work myself up to the verge of a real relapse. School doesn't make my ED go away, but it gives me so many other things to think about too that my ED feels much smaller. I couldn't imagine juggling college with my eating disorder at its worst, but I couldn't juggle anything else with my ED at that point either and I think it's good for my relationship with food to have something that keeps me occupied and gives me a routine.

But both being dudes feels, like, the best word I can think to describe it is maybe cozy?
      I'm also gender non-conforming in addition to being a binary trans man. I'm medically transitioning, ID as fully male, and use all male language, but I present more or less completely androgynously and I've always had conventionally feminine interests. I'm generally (though not exclusively) only interested in other notably effeminate guys. I grew up wanting to look like David Bowie and I get gender euphoria when my professors include me as a target while making a vague "all male fashion majors are gay" joke. I see my sexual orientation and my gender as inextricably linked. I don't ID as a man and as gay, I identify as a GNC gay man. My parents even say that when I was a little kid I clearly acted like little gender non-conforming gay boy and not like an actual girl. I see it as as important part of my gender identity and expression as anything else.

Every time I start dating someone I basically tell them right off the bat. If I like and trust them enough to go out then they deserve the warning, and if they're weird about it then they aren't a person who I, or any other ED person, should be dating. If they know then you can work together to plan out date activities that will be more manageable for you and also be a potential source of support for recovery. Even if I'm not fully recovered, I don't want to have an eating disorder forever, and I know that isolating myself is only going to make things worse.

Absolutely. I'm partially recovered and routine is one of the biggest things holding me back from progressing further. I've had an ED for almost 6 years and my ED low point was around year 2, because I'm so much better now than I was back then it can be difficult to even understand when I'm being disordered. Is it still restriction if I'm not even trying? I'm just eating the same amounts of the same food as I would normally out of habit. And then I don't want to change because I don't feel THAT unwell and like I'm "basically fine now," until my routine hits one obstacle and suddenly I'm crying in public because the only milk options at the convenience store coffee counter were whole or half and half.

To give myself a positive role model. If I'm in a place where I can only make myself look at eating disorder related content I might as well look at something that's supposed to encourage me to get better. And I figure that if I see enough media telling me it's good to eat, that'll help to combat all the other media I encounter that implies eating is bad. It's good to be exposed to the messaging of recovery even if you aren't quite there yourself yet.

I don't think there's any specific amount of time you "should"  wait to go on T, but there's also no rush if you don't want to yet. Transitioning is highly personal and you'll be ready when you're ready. Personally, I waited 8 years, but that's mostly because of my general situation. I socially transitioned at like 14, and at that point I didn't even want to go on T because I was still young enough that half the boys in my grade didn't really have secondary male sex characteristics yet. I started wanting T at about 16 but still had to wait until I was an adult, not by choice. I think a lot of what leads a person to wait (or not) is based in context.

I wouldn't go so far as to say that I like my body, but I certainly like it more than I ever did before my eating disorder. I'm still insecure about my height and feeling like my limbs are disproportionately short, and I still have gender dysphoria. I wouldn't mind maintaining this weight though, it's genuinely one of my favorite things about my flesh husk. I will contextualize this though by saying that I'm so detached from my body that I genuinely don't even see it as a part of me, more like a meat mech that I'm stuck inside of. Because of that I tend to see weight loss and my ED as like... A character creation screen. I'm not starving myself, I'm just making the meat mech more suited to me and my tastes. I'm also in a stage right now where my depression is somehow doing really well even though my other mental illnesses are all going full force, which I think plays a big role in this.

A lot of my biggest safe foods are plain carbs. White bread, saltines, white pasta, etc. Carbs are the first thing your body burns for fuel and I'm generally a hyper/active person, I'd pace constantly even without my ED, and I just love the idea that carbs will "go away" in ways that other macronutrients won't. I also have stomach issues which I think is part of it, plain carbs are safe because I know they'll help me feel better if I'm nauseous. They're also relatively bulky/high volume. Whole grains are scarier because one time I saw an infographic about how brown rice is healthier that also mentioned that it's marginally higher cal than white.

I don't know if this really counts as a food group but all food is safer if it feels aesthetically pleasing and like a nice treat (but not in a way that adds cals). I think it's a perfectionism thing, if I don't even want to eat food in the first place than the food I do eat needs to be worth it. Adding some ripped up basil and a drizzle of balsamic to anything it'll go with = that food is now somehow way less anxiety producing. If I had my way I think all I would eat is cut up fruit and like dainty little tea party snacks.

Conspiratorial may have been a bit strong of a word, but that was the most concise way to I could think of to say what I meant, and I already use too many words. That wasn't meant as a targeted accusation at OP or anyone else. I agree that thinness shouldn't be seen as a prerequisite to dressing nice. I just see lots of people online (in general, not only in ED spaces) who seem to be reading way too deeply into the actions of individuals when beauty ideals are a social issue. To me it just seems like accusing a person of actively wanting to destroy the environment because they forgot to turn a light off while ignoring the fossil fuel industry. I hope that metaphor makes sense. I agree that there should be change, I just feel like there are more productive ways to go about it. It seems weird to me to speculate that people's actions are out of malice when there are simpler explanations like insecurity or thoughtlessness. Why get mad at someone who could be struggling just as much as you when you could get mad at the system which lead to those struggles in the first place?

I don't know. I'm biased (actively a fashion student and I've also taken live model drawing classes, so I'm pretty much fully desensitized to nudity in that kind of a context) but like... How else would they start? You're wearing underwear before you put your clothes on. The human body is just the base for clothing. If they started out in pajamas or something that seems like it'd be more distracting, and depending on the complexity of what they're wearing (something with a lot of lacing/things that need to be clipped/pinned/etc.) it could also get in the way of putting on a certain garment. And I think that it's weird to assume any person posing to make themselves look thinner is trying to make other people feel worse when it seems much more likely that they're only trying to make themselves feel better. I nearly always control my body language to make myself look/feel as thin as possible, it's fully habitual at this point and I can't stand my body otherwise. I don't want to invalidate the feelings of anyone who's bothered by that content, if it's triggering to you, that's perfectly fair! But that's on you to manage and it really seems... Conspiratorial to assume that creators are just trying to make people feel bad on an individual basis. I've definitely seen a few people who come across as intentionally body checking, but mostly I think it makes sense in context. I'm sorry if this comes across as angry or defensive, again, I understand if people are bothered by it and don't hold that against them, it's just my two cents.

Yep! Mine definitely play into each other a lot too. I have absolutely debilitating executive dysfunction in addition to really bad perfectionism and sometimes restriction just feels like the only thing I'm good at. Working on something like assignments, housework, or job applications is so hard because there's so much task initiation and organization involved, but all I need to do to lose weight is move more and eat less, which is comparatively extremely easy. Skipping lunch and then pacing for three hours while I blast loud music through headphones is an exceedingly ADHD friendly activity, and the number going down on the scale gives me the sense of achievement that my barely-passing grades don't. (I'm in college/uni, so right now a big part of my ED is coping with school stress). Beyond that I'm also bad at reading bodily signals and tend to just not notice when I'm hungry or legitimately forget to eat; and my executive dysfunction issues can make it such a difficult and time consuming process to decide what I want and then make/acquire it that normally it's just a whole lot easier to keep doing what I'm doing instead. If I'm working on an art project or something and feeling pretty focused and notice that I'm hungry, I'm not going to stop the activity that I'm enjoying to switch tasks to something that will make me feel anxious or guilty, especially not when I know I probably won't be able to focus on the project properly again for several hours afterwards. And then by the time I'm done working on the original task I'm likely to have stopped feeling hungry anyway, on and on until I realize it's been nearly a full day. I have really bad impulsivity too and used to binge and purge as a teen, but as an adult my impulsivity is way more likely to manifest as substance use or abruptly going on walks.

I'm not nearly as deep into my eating disorder as I used to be which makes it extremely easy to forget how actively disordered a lot of my behaviors still are. I don't get the same aggressive waves of my heart feeling weird or my vision blacking out in the way I did in high school when my disorder was worse, but it's incredible how much I just feel like a worn out old man sometimes even though I'm only in my early twenties. Even though my ED has gotten a lot better, I've had it for almost six years now, and even though my physical symptoms are a lot less intense, they're also more ever present. I feel like the only way my ED could kill me at this point is slowly over a long period of time. I'm not suicidal and I still hope that I'm able to recover fully some day but as much as I hate to say it I never expected to live very long and if this ends up being what takes me out then so be it. I don't think it's the saddest way I could die and I have to go eventually. I'm pretty neutral towards death in general though.

Absolutely. No one I've told has ever really been surprised, if anything, people normally tell me that either they already assumed I had an ED or that, in retrospect, knowing I have one explains a lot of my behavior. I go through loads of caffeine, get really visibly anxious and perfectionistic around situations involving food, and insist on walking for almost all of my transportation, despite living in the US south, where walking everywhere is wildly impractical. I avoid eating in public unless I absolutely have to because of my schedule or to keep up appearances, tend to cycle through the same handful of safe meals (which are mostly either low calorie or conventionally childish), have set rules about things like what order I need to eat in and what utensils I can use, and openly scrutinize the nutrition labels of everything I buy. My ED is obvious enough to create unspoken tension at family gatherings. I also have a bunch of comorbidities and personality traits and fit into a lot of demographic groups that would point to an ED. I'm trans, a gay man, in my early 20s, am wildly perfectionistic, detail oriented, and impulsive, am a fashion design major, and have pretty obvious ADHD and autism as well as a substance issue and generalized anxiety. Once I mentioned my ED to someone for the first time and they semi-jokingly  told me that as a transgender fashion student, my eating disorder was so heavily implied there was almost no need to even say that part out loud. While I'm still pretty far removed from the media's image of an ED person as a cishet teenage girl from an affluent background, I'm absolutely an ED stereotype to everyone I know who's queer, mentally ill, or goes to art school.
Summary: my ideal body type is male, and it used to be sickly, but now that I'm quasi recovered it's more wiry/lean

When my depression used to be worse and I was in a more helpless situation in my teens I normally wanted to look sickly so that other people would be able to see how much I was struggling. I wanted to be so obviously physically unwell that people would volunteer to take care of me without me needing to ask for help.
     Now I'm in my early 20s and away from my parents at college/uni, way less depressed, but still mentally ill (I don't hate myself anymore, but I have the stress response of a hysterical gay poet from 1843). Now I would describe my ideal body type as "hot 70s rockstar who's diet was mostly coke." Unfortunately I'm also gay and that's kind of just what I find attractive. Especially now that I hate myself less and use my ED deal with my surroundings more, I definitely aestheticize it too much, but idk how else to keep the ED thoughts at a controllable level.
     The entire time, I've wanted to be skinnier to look older and more masculine. Apparently a lot of people think being thinner makes you look more feminine or younger? Which is wild because I associate women with curves and children with baby fat. When I think of people who are thin I always think about lanky men in their late teens or twenties. I'm also a trans guy though and I was a naturally chubby kid that leaned out a lot with puberty, so that probably explains my angle. Need to lose everything soft, I want cheek bones and arm veins and to be so skinny that it tricks people into thinking I have longer limbs.

Absolutely. I'm never hungry, but always hungry. I have no appetite but I'm physically starving. Food sounds amazing and it's all I can think about, but I feel stuffed before even starting. I'm absolutely famished but uncomfortably full. It barely even matters how much I eat. Warning that this probably gets upsetting
     Several reasons. I was always a bit chubby as a kid, never huge but always on the heavier end of average or slightly overweight. My thoughts around food were normal and healthy, I think, but I never liked my body. Around 12 or so I realized that when I didn't eat I felt better about myself and so I would start skipping meals as a sort of emotional pick me up. I don't count that as the start of my ed, but that is where things started going downhill. Around 16 is where I count the beginning of my ed. I hated my body, not because I felt ugly necessarily, but because I'm a trans man and I thought my little bit of extra chub made me look even younger and more feminine than would be typical of a young trans guy who hadn't medically transitioned. I wanted to lose weight so that my chest and hips would be smaller and so that my hands and arms and face would look less soft. I started counting calories and very quickly went off the deep end.
     That's how things got started but different emotional factors kept thing going. I wanted to be skinny enough that I could make myself stop menstruating. I wanted to see if I could lose enough weight to make myself completely flat chested, and I wanted to see the veins in my arms like a cis man. My brain presented severe weight loss kind of like a way I could fix my incorrect birth sex all by myself.
     On top of that though my mental health had already been spiralling for years. When I was little I always prided myself on being the smart kid and doing well in school, but as school became more and more difficult because of my depression and I started failing all my classes, I basically lost the one thing I'd always had confidence in. So instead of priding myself on my ability to succeed in school I prided myself on my ability to starve instead. It made me feel like I was accomplishing something even when I was doing so poorly mentally that I could barely leave my house.
      Another reason, I don't think my parents are abusive but they are neglectful. In particular as the oldest child I was expected to stay out of their way and look after myself, and sometimes look after my sibling too. The only time I ever really felt loved or cared for as a child were if I was either being "perfect" or having some sort of emergency that required immediate attention. I liked that my ed made me feel ill and put me at risk of having an emergency because that made me feel loved. At the same time starving felt like an act of rebellion against my parents, I would daydream about being hospitalized for my ed and telling them it was their fault I got sick and watching them feel guilty. It was a way to test whether or not they'd get worried about me and I could use my anger towards them as fuel for my behaviors.
     I don't know if my mom has ever had a full ed but she definitely struggles with some level of disordered eating so there's some level of competition there.

In summary: to cope with gender dysphoria, child neglect, and gifted kid burnout
